articles.content_en: Article 13 A network data processor that conducts network data processing activities that affect or may affect national security shall undergo a national security review in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 14 Where a network data processor needs to transfer network data due to merger, division, dissolution, bankruptcy or other reasons, the recipient of the network data shall continue to perform the obligation of network data security protection.

Article 15 Where a State organ commissions another person to construct, operate or maintain an e-government system, or to store or process government data, it shall undergo strict approval procedures in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, specify the network data processing authority and protection responsibilities of the entrusted party, and supervise the entrusted party in fulfilling its obligations of network data security protection.

Article 16 A network data processor that provides services to State organs or operators of critical information infrastructure, or participates in the construction, operation or maintenance of other public infrastructure or public service systems, shall perform the obligation of network data security protection in accordance with laws, regulations and contractual stipulations, and provide safe, stable and continuous services.
A network data processor as mentioned in the preceding paragraph shall not, without the consent of the commissioning party, access, obtain, retain, use, disclose or provide network data to others, and shall not conduct correlation analysis on network data.

Article 17 An information system that provides services to State organs shall strengthen network data security management by reference to the management requirements for e-government systems, and ensure network data security.

Article 18 A network data processor that uses automated tools to access or collect network data shall assess the impact on network services, shall not illegally intrude into another person's network, and shall not interfere with the normal operation of network services.

Article 19 A network data processor that provides generative artificial intelligence services shall strengthen the security management of training data and training data processing activities, and take effective measures to prevent and handle network data security risks.

Article 20 A network data processor that provides products or services to the public shall accept public supervision, establish convenient channels for complaints and reports on network data security, publish information such as the methods for complaints and reports, and promptly accept and handle such complaints and reports.

Article 23 Where an individual requests to access, copy, correct, supplement, delete, or restrict the processing of his or her personal information, or cancels an account or withdraws consent, the network data processor shall accept the request promptly and provide convenient methods and channels to support the individual in exercising his or her rights, and shall not impose unreasonable conditions to restrict the individual's reasonable requests.

Article 24 Where, due to the use of automated collection technology or other reasons, non-essential personal information or personal information for which the individual's consent has not been obtained according to law is unavoidably collected, or where an individual cancels an account, the network data processor shall delete the personal information or anonymize it. Where the retention period prescribed by laws or administrative regulations has not yet expired, or where deletion or anonymization of personal information is technically infeasible, the network data processor shall cease processing other than storage and the adoption of necessary security protection measures.

Article 26 Where a network data processor outside the territory of the People's Republic of China processes personal information of domestic natural persons and, in accordance with Article 53 of the Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, establishes a specialized institution or appoints a representative within the territory, it shall report the name of such institution or the name and contact information of such representative to the local cyberspace administration at the city with districts level; the cyberspace administration shall promptly inform the relevant competent authority at the same level.

Article 27 A network data processor shall periodically conduct a compliance audit on its processing of personal information in accordance with laws and administrative regulations, either by itself or by entrusting a professional institution.

Article 28 A network data processor that processes personal information of 10 million or more persons shall also comply with the provisions of Articles 30 and 32 of these Regulations regarding network data processors that process important data (hereinafter referred to as processors of important data).

Article 29 The national coordination mechanism for data security work shall coordinate relevant authorities in formulating a catalog of important data and strengthen the protection of important data. All regions and departments shall, in accordance with the data classification and graded protection system, determine the specific catalog of important data in their respective regions, departments and related industries and fields, and provide focused protection for network data included in the catalog.
A network data processor shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, identify and declare important data. Where data is confirmed as important data, the relevant region or department shall promptly notify the network data processor or make a public announcement. The network data processor shall fulfill its responsibility for network data security protection.
The State encourages network data processors to use technologies and products such as data labeling to enhance the level of security management of important data.

Article 32 Where a processor of important data, due to merger, division, dissolution, bankruptcy or other reasons, may affect the security of important data, it shall take measures to ensure network data security and report to the relevant competent authority at or above the provincial level the plan for disposition of important data, and the name or title and contact information of the recipient, etc.; if the competent authority is not clear, it shall report to the data security work coordination mechanism at or above the provincial level.

Article 34 The national cyberspace administration shall coordinate relevant authorities in establishing a special working mechanism for national data cross-border security management, studying and formulating relevant policies for national network data cross-border security management, and coordinating the handling of major matters concerning network data cross-border security.

Article 36 Where an international treaty or agreement concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China provides for the conditions for providing personal information abroad, such provisions may be followed.

Article 37 Where important data collected and generated during operations within the territory of the People's Republic of China by a network data processor truly needs to be provided abroad, the processor shall undergo the data cross-border security assessment organized by the national cyberspace administration. Where a network data processor identifies and declares important data in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, but such data has not been notified to the processor or publicly announced as important data by the relevant region or department, the processor is not required to declare it as important data for the data cross-border security assessment.

Article 38 After passing the data cross-border security assessment, a network data processor that provides personal information and important data abroad shall not exceed the purpose, method, scope, type, scale, etc. of data cross-border transfer as specified at the time of assessment.

Article 39 The State takes measures to prevent and handle cross-border network data security risks and threats. No individual or organization shall provide programs, tools, etc. specifically used to destroy or circumvent technical measures; and where knowing that another person engages in activities such as destroying or circumventing technical measures, shall not provide technical support or assistance to such person.

Article 40 A network platform service provider shall specify through platform rules or contracts the network data security protection obligations of third-party product and service providers that access its platform, and urge such third-party providers to strengthen network data security management.
The preceding paragraph shall apply to producers of devices such as smart terminals with pre-installed applications.
Where a third-party product or service provider violates the provisions of laws or administrative regulations, or the platform rules or contractual stipulations, in conducting network data processing activities, and causes harm to users, the network platform service provider, the third-party product or service provider, and the producer of devices such as smart terminals with pre-installed applications shall bear corresponding liability according to law.
The State encourages insurance companies to develop insurance types for liability for network data damage, and encourages network platform service providers and producers of devices such as smart terminals with pre-installed applications to take out such insurance.

Article 41 A network platform service provider that provides application distribution services shall establish application verification rules and conduct verification related to network data security. Where it discovers that an application to be distributed or already distributed does not comply with the provisions of laws or administrative regulations, or the mandatory requirements of national standards, it shall take measures such as warning, refusal to distribute, suspension of distribution, or termination of distribution.

Article 42 Where a network platform service provider pushes information to individuals through automated decision-making, it shall set up an option to close personalized recommendations that is easy to understand, access and operate, and provide users with functions such as refusing to receive pushed information and deleting user tags targeted at their personal characteristics.

Article 43 The State promotes the construction of public services for network identity authentication, and conducts promotion and application in accordance with the principles of government guidance and user voluntariness.
Network platform service providers are encouraged to support users in using the national network identity authentication public service to register and verify their real identity information.

Article 44 A large network platform service provider shall publish an annual social responsibility report on personal information protection, the content of which includes but is not limited to the personal information protection measures and their effectiveness, the status of accepting applications for individuals to exercise their rights, and the performance of duties by a personal information protection supervisory body mainly composed of external members.

Article 45 A large network platform service provider that provides network data across borders shall comply with the national requirements for data cross-border security management, improve relevant technical and management measures, and prevent cross-border network data security risks.

Article 47 The national cyberspace administration is responsible for coordinating network data security and related supervision and management.
Public security organs and State security organs shall, in accordance with relevant laws, administrative regulations and the provisions of these Regulations, undertake the responsibility for supervision and management of network data security within their respective functions, and prevent and combat illegal and criminal activities that jeopardize network data security according to law.
The national data management department shall fulfill corresponding network data security responsibilities in the concrete performance of data management work.
All regions and departments shall be responsible for the network data collected and generated in their respective work and for network data security.

Article 48 All relevant competent authorities shall assume the responsibility for supervision and management of network data security in their respective industries and fields, designate a working body for network data security protection in their respective industries and fields, coordinate the formulation and organization of implementation of emergency response plans for network data security incidents in their respective industries and fields, periodically organize risk assessments on network data security in their respective industries and fields, supervise and inspect the performance of network data security protection obligations by network data processors, and guide and urge network data processors to timely rectify existing risks and hidden dangers.

Article 49 The national cyberspace administration shall coordinate relevant competent authorities in promptly summarizing, assessing, sharing and publishing information related to network data security risks, and strengthen the sharing of network data security information, monitoring and early warning of network data security risks and threats, and emergency response to network data security incidents.

Article 51 When conducting network data security supervision and inspection, the relevant competent authority shall be objective and impartial, and shall not charge fees to the entity under inspection.
In the course of network data security supervision and inspection, the relevant competent authority shall not access or collect business information unrelated to network data security, and the information obtained may only be used for the needs of maintaining network data security; it shall not be used for other purposes.
Where the relevant competent authority discovers that the network data processing activities of a network data processor pose a significant security risk, it may, in accordance with the prescribed authority and procedures, require the network data processor to suspend relevant services, modify platform rules, improve technical measures, etc., to eliminate network data security risks.

Article 52 When conducting network data security supervision and inspection, the relevant competent authorities shall strengthen coordination, cooperation and information communication, and reasonably determine the frequency and method of inspection to avoid unnecessary inspections and overlapping or duplicate inspections.
Personal information protection compliance audits, risk assessments of important data, security assessments for cross-border transfer of important data, etc., shall be better coordinated to avoid duplicate assessments or audits. Where the contents of risk assessment of important data and network security grading assessment overlap, the relevant results may be mutually accepted.

Article 53 The relevant competent authority and its staff members shall keep confidential, according to law, the network data such as personal privacy, personal information, trade secrets and confidential business information known to them in the performance of their duties, and shall not disclose or illegally provide such data to others.

Article 54 Where an overseas organization or individual engages in network data processing activities that endanger the national security or public interest of the People's Republic of China, or infringe upon the personal information rights and interests of citizens of the People's Republic of China, the national cyberspace administration, together with the relevant competent authority, may take corresponding necessary measures according to law.

Article 55 Whoever violates the provisions of Article 12, Articles 16 to 20, Article 22, paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 40, Article 41, or Article 42 of these Regulations shall be ordered by the cyberspace, telecommunications, public security or other competent authority, in accordance with their respective functions, to make corrections, be given a warning, and have the illegal gains confiscated; if the violator refuses to make corrections or if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not more than 1 million yuan shall be imposed, and the violator may be ordered to suspend relevant business, suspend operations for rectification, have the relevant business permit revoked, or have the business license revoked; the directly responsible supervisor and other directly liable persons may be fined not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan.

Article 56 Whoever violates the provisions of Article 13 of these Regulations shall be ordered by the cyberspace, telecommunications, public security, State security or other competent authority, in accordance with their respective functions, to make corrections, be given a warning, and may be concurrently fined not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 1 million yuan; the directly responsible supervisor and other directly liable persons may be fined not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan; if the violator refuses to make corrections or if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 1 million yuan but not more than 10 million yuan shall be imposed, and the violator may be ordered to suspend relevant business, suspend operations for rectification, have the relevant business permit revoked, or have the business license revoked; the directly responsible supervisor and other directly liable persons shall be fined not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 1 million yuan.

Article 57 Whoever violates the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 29, paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 30, Article 31, or Article 32 of these Regulations shall be ordered by the cyberspace, telecommunications, public security or other competent authority, in accordance with their respective functions, to make corrections, be given a warning, and may be concurrently fined not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan; the directly responsible supervisor and other directly liable persons may be fined not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan; if the violator refuses to make corrections or if serious consequences such as a massive data leak occur, a fine of not less than 500,000 yuan but not more than 2 million yuan shall be imposed, and the violator may be ordered to suspend relevant business, suspend operations for rectification, have the relevant business permit revoked, or have the business license revoked; the directly responsible supervisor and other directly liable persons shall be fined not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan.

Article 58 Whoever violates other relevant provisions of these Regulations shall be investigated for legal liability by the relevant competent authority in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China, the Data Security Law of the People's Republic of China, the Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China and other laws.

Article 59 Where a network data processor proactively eliminates or mitigates the harmful consequences of an illegal act, or the illegal act is minor and promptly corrected without causing harmful consequences, or is a first-time violation with minor harmful consequences and promptly corrected, the administrative penalty shall be mitigated or reduced, or no administrative penalty shall be imposed, in accordance with the provisions of the Administrative Penalty Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 60 Where a State organ fails to perform the obligation of network data security protection as provided in these Regulations, its superior organ or the relevant competent authority shall order it to make corrections; the directly responsible supervisor and other directly liable persons shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 61 Whoever violates these Regulations and causes harm to others shall bear civil liability according to law; if the act constitutes a violation of public security administration, a public security administration penalty shall be imposed according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 62 For the purposes of these Regulations, the following terms have the meanings set forth below:
(1) "Network data" means various electronic data processed and generated through networks.
(2) "Network data processing activities" means activities such as collection, storage, use, processing, transmission, provision, disclosure and deletion of network data.
(3) "Network data processor" means an individual or organization that independently decides the purpose and method of processing in network data processing activities.
(4) "Important data" means data in specific domains, specific groups, specific regions, or reaching a certain precision and scale that, once tampered with, destroyed, disclosed, illegally obtained or illegally used, may directly endanger national security, economic operation, social stability, public health and safety.
(5) "Entrusted processing" means network data processing activities carried out by a network data processor through entrusting an individual or organization to process data in accordance with agreed purposes and methods.
(6) "Joint processing" means network data processing activities in which two or more network data processors jointly decide the purpose and method of processing network data.
(7) "Separate consent" means specific and explicit consent given by an individual specifically for a particular processing of his or her personal information.
(8) "Large network platform" means a network platform with 50 million or more registered users or 10 million or more monthly active users, with complex business types, and whose network data processing activities have a significant impact on national security, economic operation, national welfare and people's livelihood.

Article 63 Network data processing activities involving core data shall be carried out in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.
Where a natural person processes personal information for personal or family affairs, these Regulations shall not apply.
For network data processing activities involving State secrets or work secrets, the provisions of laws and administrative regulations such as the Law of the People's Republic of China on Guarding State Secrets shall apply.
Article 64 These Regulations shall come into force as of January 1, 2025.
